stories.title: Stronger flu shots linked to lower Alzheimer's risk
stories.summary: Researchers at UTHealth Houston found that adults aged 65 and older who received a high-dose flu vaccine had a 55% lower risk of developing Alzheimer's disease. Standard-dose vaccines were associated with a 40% reduction. The study analyzed data from nearly 200,000 patients.

stories.title: Alkaline phosphatase trial fails to prevent kidney injury
stories.summary: A phase 2 trial of the drug ilofotase alfa found it did not significantly reduce acute kidney injury in 204 high-risk patients undergoing cardiac surgery. The condition complicates up to 30 percent of on-pump procedures and currently lacks any approved pharmacological prevention methods.

stories.title: Lipoprotein(a) drug shows no impact on cardiac events
stories.summary: Reducing elevated levels of lipoprotein(a) with the drug pelacarsen had no effect on cardiovascular events in patients with pre-existing heart disease, according to the Lp(a)HORIZON trial. Investigators noted the results were unexpected, though they maintained it is not the end of the story for the therapy.

stories.title: Women with Parkinson's show higher Alzheimer's plaque burden
stories.summary: A Mayo Clinic autopsy study found women with Parkinson's disease are more than twice as likely as men to carry a high burden of Alzheimer's-associated amyloid plaques. The findings suggest a need for sex-specific strategies for managing Parkinson's dementia, a condition that currently lacks disease-modifying therapies.

stories.title: Gene-silencing therapy lowers cholesterol and triglycerides
stories.summary: A Cleveland Clinic study presented at the American Heart Association sessions found a single dose of ARO-DIMER-PA lowered both LDL cholesterol and triglycerides. Study author Luke Laffin stated the drug successfully blocks two separate disease pathways in the liver at once.

stories.title: Pelacarsen trial misses primary cardiovascular endpoint
stories.summary: The Phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial found that while pelacarsen reduced lipoprotein(a) levels by 78.4% after one year, it did not reduce major cardiovascular events. Patients taking the drug experienced heart attacks and strokes at nearly the same rate as those receiving a placebo.

stories.title: Pelacarsen trial results show no reduction in heart events
stories.summary: A Cleveland Clinic-led trial of 4.7 years found that the drug pelacarsen successfully lowered lipoprotein(a) but failed to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with pre-existing heart disease. The drug was also associated with mild side effects and rare allergic reactions.

stories.title: Heart disease drug fails in clinical trial
stories.summary: An experimental drug intended to prevent heart attacks and strokes failed to protect volunteers in a major study. Cleveland Clinic cardiologist Steven Nissen, who led the trial, said he was shocked by the results. Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in developed countries.

stories.title: Anti-inflammatory trial yields neutral findings
stories.summary: Findings from the ZEUS phase 3 clinical trial suggest that targeting inflammation to reduce cardiovascular risk is less straightforward than previously thought. The study, led by Mass General Brigham researchers, indicates that the relationship between inflammation and heart disease requires further investigation.

stories.title: AIIMS Raipur performs rare surgery for parasitic lung disease
stories.summary: Doctors at AIIMS Raipur removed multiple parasitic cysts from the pulmonary artery of a 24-year-old woman. The procedure, which preserved the patient's lung, is rare, with only 16 such surgically treated cases reported worldwide. The patient faced a potentially fatal complication that could have required organ removal.

stories.title: Kidney transplant study finds no longevity benefit from rapamycin
stories.summary: A real-world evaluation of national transplant registry data found that long-term prescription of rapamycin did not improve patient longevity compared to alternative immunosuppressive regimens. The study analyzed thousands of adult kidney transplant recipients who had survived with a functioning graft for at least one year.

stories.title: Bariatric surgery effective after GLP-1 agonist failure
stories.summary: A study published in the Annals of Surgery reports that bariatric surgery is associated with clinically meaningful weight loss in patients who failed to respond to or could not tolerate semaglutide or tirzepatide. The findings suggest surgery as a rescue strategy for weight management.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir receives two AIIMS facilities
stories.summary: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated a new modular operation theatre complex at AIIMS Jammu. The minister stated that Jammu and Kashmir is the only Union Territory to receive two AIIMS facilities, citing the intervention of the Prime Minister in the region's healthcare infrastructure development.

stories.title: Dual malnutrition burden rises in Indian households
stories.summary: A study found that the co-existence of underweight or stunted children and overweight mothers in the same household doubled between 2005 and 2021. Researchers identified this as a growing malnutrition paradox, noting a clear socio-demographic pattern in how these conflicting forms of malnutrition emerge.

stories.title: AIIMS warns of systemic health risks from Delhi air
stories.summary: Senior doctors at AIIMS warn that Delhi's air pollution poses risks to the heart, brain, and kidneys, rather than just the lungs. Fine particulate matter known as PM2.5 can enter the bloodstream after reaching the lungs, according to former pulmonary department head Professor G.C. Khilnani.

stories.title: Former AIIMS director warns of rising health risks
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. A former AIIMS director has issued warnings regarding the health impact of worsening air quality in Delhi ahead of Diwali, noting that even healthy individuals are experiencing illness as pollution levels rise.

stories.title: FICCI calls for health-led approach to clean air
stories.summary: A FICCI-EY paper argues that India requires a health-led approach to clean air with explicit reduction targets for PM2.5. The report notes that air pollution was attributable to more than two million deaths in 2023 and impacts healthcare expenditure and national productivity.

stories.title: National Health Authority reviews Ayushman Bharat progress
stories.summary: The National Health Authority concluded a two-day review of the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. Discussions focused on expanding beneficiary coverage, improving healthcare delivery, and accelerating the adoption of digital health services across states and union territories.

stories.title: Supreme Court calls vehicular emissions a major pollution factor in Delhi-NCR
stories.summary: The Supreme Court identified vehicular emissions as a primary driver of air pollution in Delhi-NCR, citing the need for immediate and long-term interventions. With the air quality index reaching 400, the Bench expressed concern over persistent traffic congestion. The court continues to discuss the issue.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes microbial monitoring updates
stories.summary: The Health and Family Welfare Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules 1945 to align microbial monitoring in sterile manufacturing areas with World Health Organization guidelines. The update mandates that any detected microbial growth in critical Grade A zones must trigger a formal investigation.

stories.title: India highlights health infrastructure scale at UNGA81
stories.summary: India showcased its network of 1.8 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and 900 million health IDs at the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava reaffirmed the country's commitment to universal health coverage and protecting citizens from financial hardship through primary and tertiary care.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat scheme adds 4.2 crore enrollees
stories.summary: The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana added 4.2 crore enrollees over the past three months, with 2.2 lakh beneficiaries receiving treatment. The National Health Authority confirmed the figures during a review meeting in Kolkata, noting the scheme's role in financial protection and digital health empowerment.

stories.title: National Health Authority reviews scheme implementation
stories.summary: The National Health Authority convened a two-day review meeting in Kolkata to assess the progress of the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. Senior officials from states and territories gathered to deliberate on strategies for strengthening implementation in the coming phase.

stories.title: Hospitals prepare for Diwali emergency surge
stories.summary: Emergency departments are bracing for the annual increase in firecracker-related injuries, burns, and respiratory distress as Diwali celebrations begin. Trauma specialists and pulmonologists are preparing for the expected influx of patients, noting that the festive period often results in a predictable but difficult surge in medical emergencies.

stories.title: Houthi-run ministry reports 33 killed in airstrikes
stories.summary: At least 33 people were killed and 39 wounded in airstrikes near Sanaa, according to the Houthi-run Saba news agency. The report follows the resumption of hostilities between Saudi-led forces and the group. Saudi Arabia stated it is investigating the report. The 2022 UN-brokered truce remains shattered.

stories.title: Sennar reports decline in dengue fever cases
stories.summary: The Sennar Health Ministry has reported a decline in dengue fever cases. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Palestinian Health Minister appeals for Gaza aid
stories.summary: Palestinian Health Minister Majed Abu Ramadan has appealed for international intervention as winter rains submerge displacement tents in Gaza. The minister warned of deteriorating health conditions and mounting risks of infectious diseases, urging the United Nations and relief organizations to act to save the displaced population.

stories.title: US measles cases reach 35-year high
stories.summary: The United States has recorded over 5,000 measles cases this year, marking the highest total in 35 years. The figure was released in an official count on Friday. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: RFK Jr. says cyclosporiasis outbreak is under control
stories.summary: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. stated that the multi-state cyclosporiasis outbreak, which has sickened at least 1,600 people, is under control. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is currently investigating the parasitic illness alongside federal and local partners.

stories.title: Alaska health officials issue mpox advisory
stories.summary: State health officials in Alaska have issued an advisory following a new outbreak of mpox in Anchorage. The contagious viral disease, which saw a global outbreak in 2022, is currently emerging in the state's largest city.

stories.title: Gaza Health Ministry calls for investigation into congenital anomalies
stories.summary: The Gaza Health Ministry has called for an investigation into rising cases of congenital anomalies. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: WHO adds Ebola vaccine candidates to efficacy trial
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has recommended adding Moderna and Oxford-developed vaccine candidates to the Tumaini ring vaccination trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This marks the first time vaccines specifically targeting the Bundibugyo virus will be evaluated in a controlled efficacy trial during an outbreak.

stories.title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak impacts adult population
stories.summary: Pennsylvania is seeing a high proportion of measles cases among adults, presenting unique diagnostic challenges for medical professionals. Infectious disease experts noted that the current situation differs from historical patterns, as the state manages its worst outbreak in over three decades.

stories.title: Measles outbreak continues in Pennsylvania
stories.summary: Pennsylvania has recorded over 1,400 measles cases and six deaths in 2026. Health officials continue to issue exposure alerts for public spaces, including schools and hospitals. While two doses of the MMR vaccine are cited as 97 percent effective, the state remains in the midst of its worst outbreak.

stories.title: Health Ministry monitors Ebola situation in Central Africa
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is monitoring the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Officials from the National Centre for Disease Control have initiated precautionary measures, though the ministry clarified there are currently no reports of the virus in India.

stories.title: Burnham 10-year plan faces potential delay
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed that his 10-year plan for Britain may be delayed until January. Initially promised for later this year, the document was expected to serve as the core policy statement for the administration. The government has not provided a revised release date.

stories.title: Low-cost cancer care app pilot costs under 0.1% of Karnataka's health budget
stories.summary: A mobile app for chemotherapy scheduling and care coordination was piloted for roughly US$1,205, according to Discover Public Health. The sum represents 0.093% of Karnataka's annual budget for its national cancer and disease control programme. The study provides rare cost data for mHealth in resource-constrained settings.

stories.title: AIIMS Bibinagar launches patient app to manage hospital queues
stories.summary: The All India Institute of Medical Sciences in Bibinagar has released a mobile app for appointment booking, test payments and report downloads. The institute introduced the service to reduce morning crowds at its registration and laboratory counters. The app is available on major mobile platforms.

stories.title: India digital health market projected to reach USD 90 billion by 2034
stories.summary: India's digital health market is expected to reach USD 90 billion by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 18.06 percent. The sector features a competitive mix of telehealth specialists, health analytics firms and startups, with participants differentiating through AI capabilities and cloud-based platforms. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Altera Digital Health to cut 133 roles in New York
stories.summary: Software vendor Altera Digital Health will lay off 133 employees at its Melville office starting December 31, 2026. The company filed a formal notice with the New York State Department of Labor, citing the expiration of client contracts as the reason for the permanent job reductions.

stories.title: ICMR mental health platform wins national e-governance award
stories.summary: The ICMR-MINDS platform has received a Gold Award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026. The platform uses artificial intelligence to improve access to mental healthcare services. The award recognises the initiative for its innovation in providing citizen-centric services through new age technologies.

stories.title: Nicklaus Children’s Health System receives digital health recognition
stories.summary: The College of Healthcare Information Management Executives has awarded Nicklaus Children’s Health System a Level 9 achievement in its 2026 Digital Health Most Wired Survey. The system ranked above peers in areas including cybersecurity, data management and patient engagement among more than 44,000 facilities surveyed.

stories.title: Tripura to transition government hospitals to paperless operations
stories.summary: Tripura will move all government hospitals to paperless operations starting November 10, 2026. The state recently showcased its digital health model at a national review meeting in Kolkata. The transition is part of a broader effort to modernise public healthcare and expand digital services.

stories.title: Umbrella review examines digital health tools for patient engagement
stories.summary: A new review in PLOS Digital Health examines whether smartphone apps and telehealth platforms improve patient engagement. The analysis of studies through June 2025 notes that evidence remains fragmented across populations and modalities. The researchers aimed to determine if these tools actually improve self-management and medication adherence.

stories.title: Health Minister sets March 2027 completion for AIIMS Awantipora
stories.summary: Union Health Minister JP Nadda has directed officials to accelerate construction at AIIMS Awantipora. Outpatient services are targeted to begin before December 2026, with inpatient services proposed for July 2027. The minister reviewed infrastructure progress and medical equipment procurement during a recent site visit.

stories.title: Moderate coffee consumption linked to lower anxiety risk
stories.summary: A study of 460,000 adults in the UK Biobank found that moderate coffee drinkers were the least likely to develop anxiety and depression over 13 years. Researchers identified a sweet spot for intake that correlates with mood benefits. The relationship between caffeine and the nervous system remains complex.

stories.title: Study links motor cortex plasticity to depression severity
stories.summary: Research published in BMC Medicine identifies impaired neuroplasticity in the primary motor cortex as a marker for depression severity. The study suggests this impairment could serve as an index of cortical dysfunction, while noting that adjunctive acupuncture may help enhance treatment efficacy in moderate cases.

stories.title: Cyberbullying linked to lower life satisfaction in adolescents
stories.summary: A study of 183,928 adolescents across 42 countries found that cyberbullying is associated with lower life satisfaction and increased psychological symptoms. The research examined how teacher and peer support moderate these outcomes. The findings were published in BMC Public Health using data from the 2017/2018 school-aged survey.

stories.title: Global mental health worsening as young people struggle, study shows - The Eastleigh Voice
stories.summary: Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue Global mental health worsening as young people struggle, study shows The Eastleigh Voice The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now.

stories.title: Evening chronotype associated with inflammatory skin disease
stories.summary: Adults who prefer evening hours report higher stress and lower psychological quality of life if they have inflammatory skin diseases like psoriasis or dermatitis. A study of the EPISONO-2018 data found these participants also reported more depressive symptoms. The findings appear in Archives of Dermatological Research.

stories.title: Behavioral health training linked to reduced clinician stigma
stories.summary: Primary care clinicians who completed a structured behavioral health training program reported lower mental health stigma than untrained peers. A study of 154 providers found that targeted education in psychiatry may improve attitudes toward patients. Socioeconomic factors of the practice location showed no relationship with stigma levels.

stories.title: Israelis in distress turn to generative AI for support
stories.summary: A study from Tel Hai College suggests that nearly half of Israeli users experiencing severe psychological distress turn to generative AI for emotional support. Researchers warn the technology may act as a digital bandage that deepens isolation. The software is currently providing the comfort it is programmed to simulate.

stories.title: Seasonal affective disorder and the winter blues
stories.summary: The winter blues describe low energy and mood changes as days grow shorter and colder. This seasonal shift is formally recognized as seasonal affective disorder. The condition remains a common response to the reduction of daylight hours during the transition into the winter months.

stories.title: Ketamine assisted mindfulness for opioid cravings
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine found that adding ketamine to mindfulness treatment may help patients recognize body signals. These changes could assist in reducing opioid cravings. The study suggests a potential path for therapy, though further clinical evidence is required.

stories.title: Give an Hour releases Veteran MILE case study
stories.summary: Give an Hour released a case study on Veteran MILE, an initiative designed to improve mental health literacy and peer support. The program is aligned with CDC Foundation best practices. It aims to shift mental health training from individual learning toward broader organizational capacity within veteran serving groups.

stories.title: Unpredictable home environments linked to mental health risks
stories.summary: A study in Nature Mental Health found that unpredictable childhood experiences are linked to mental health risks even when abuse or neglect are not present. A five question screen identified these risks in children missed by standard adversity questionnaires. Identifying instability may help broaden current screening efforts.

stories.title: Repeat brain injuries linked to higher mental health risks
stories.summary: A new study indicates that individuals who sustain repeat brain injuries face higher risks for mental health issues. The research highlights a connection between repeated trauma and long term psychological outcomes. The full piece is for subscribers.

research.title: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
research.summary: A surprising discovery reveals how psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, rapidly reshapes the brain by creating new neural connections and strengthening them. Researchers found that the drug behaves differently in healthy and chronically stressed mice, potentially helping repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. Most intriguingly.

research.title: A compound hidden in broccoli could help fight a devastating genetic disease
research.summary: A compound naturally found in broccoli could help fight Friedreich ataxia, a devastating genetic disease that progressively damages the nervous system, by boosting a vital protein and protecting nerve cells. Scientists hope the discovery could lead to an affordable treatment, although clinical trials are still needed to establish.
